validator: draft 1 passes with no problems, soft points or warnings
keep: The idea is named up front: diodes pointed the right ways steer both halves of the AC the same way through a load, giving DC that pulses.

The picture is the brief's rectifier bench: a switch for half-wave, bridge and six-pulse, a dragged time cursor, conducting diodes bold with the current's path and an arrow through the load, the output and its area-over-length average building under the cursor (0.318, 0.637, 1.35 times), and a probe on a blocked diode peaking at the PIV.

Every number is computed from a shown rule: 325 V peak, 104 V half-wave, 207 V bridge, 1.4 V of two drops, 490 V six-pulse dip from cos 30 degrees, 3 / pi and 3 root 2 / pi giving 540 V and 594 V. Only 0.637, 100 Hz, 0.7 V and the PIV failure carry footnotes.
Both brief misconceptions get a DO screen with its own hint: current backwards or the second pair idle (screen 4), and a blocked diode seeing nothing (screen 8).
Thirteen screens, SHOW 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 alternating with DO 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, ending on two mixed puzzles (an open bridge diode, 440 V six-pulse). SHOW screens run 71 to 89 words.
The diode's 0.7 V is not idealised away: screen 6 shows why 1.4 V matters on a 12 V charger and not on 207 V.
The analogy comes from Dan's own trade (an intermediate switch), not from water, and differs from lesson 1's non-return valve.
fix: Causal step skipped: the six-pulse rule says the highest line drives the positive rail but not why the other upper diodes block. Say the positive rail can sit no lower than the highest line, so every other upper diode is pushed backwards (screen 9 and explain).
Check tests recall: screen 8 asks for the 325 V that screen 7 has just stated. Move it to a new case, a 115 V single-phase bridge, so he works out the 163 V peak himself.
Answer given away: screen 11's Read states 594 V on 440 V, which is screen 13's answer. Drop it from the Read.
Explain names wire A and the positive half without saying which wire is high in the positive half. Say wire A is the high one first.
Analogy is loose: an intermediate switch does not cross the wires 'each half cycle'; it swaps between straight and crossed. Say so, and that the bridge does it by itself at each zero crossing.
Unreadable label: the readout 'Probe, reverse across diode' is clumsy. Call it 'Probe on the diode'.
